ai.definition: Cognitive RPA Agents are advanced software robots that utilize large language models (LLMs) to handle unstructured data, make decisions, and perform tasks with a higher level of autonomy than traditional robotic process automation (RPA).
ai.howItWorks: These agents integrate robust natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and computer vision capabilities into RPA frameworks. They can interpret complex screen content, understand context, and execute decision-making processes that were previously difficult for rule-based RPA to handle.
ai.problemSolved: Cognitive RPA Agents address the limitations of traditional RPA by enabling automation in scenarios with unstructured data, dynamic user interfaces, and more complex business logic. They reduce the need for extensive coding and manual configuration, making it easier to automate a wider range of tasks.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing and training LLMs, integrating them into RPA frameworks, and testing the agents in controlled environments before deployment.
ai.buildProcess: Developers train models on large datasets, fine-tune them for specific use cases, and integrate these models with existing RPA tools. This includes creating pipelines that can handle unstructured data inputs and generate appropriate actions based on context.
ai.costDrivers: Costs are driven by the complexity of model training, data labeling, and integration efforts. The ongoing costs include maintenance, updates to models, and potential cloud infrastructure expenses for hosting and running these agents.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: growing adoption in enterprise settings as businesses seek more flexible automation solutions.
ai.regulation: Currently, there is no specific regulation targeting cognitive RPA agents. However, compliance with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR) and ethical guidelines for AI use are critical considerations.
ai.risks: Risks include model bias, data privacy concerns, and potential misuse of the technology. There is also a risk of over-reliance on these agents without proper human oversight.
ai.profitability: Profitability depends on the specific implementation and industry. Early adopters in sectors with complex workflows can see significant cost savings and efficiency gains, but widespread adoption requires further development to reduce costs and improve performance.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments will likely focus on improving model accuracy, reducing training time, enhancing explainability, and expanding use cases beyond current limitations.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and data center operations. Cloud-based agents can have higher power consumption depending on the cloud provider's infrastructure.

glossary.def: Large Language Model, a type of machine learning model trained to understand and generate human-like text.
Robotic Process Automation, software technology used in business process automation that automates routine tasks through the use of software robots or 'bots'.
Natural Language Processing, a field of artificial intelligence concerned with making computers understand and generate human language.

subsystems.name: UI automation layer
subsystems.role: drives real applications — browsers, desktop apps, terminals — the way a person would.

subsystems.name: Perception layer
subsystems.role: turns messy inputs into text and structure a model can reason over.

subsystems.name: Reasoning and planning
subsystems.role: decides what to do next: decompose the task, pick a tool, check the result.

subsystems.name: Knowledge retrieval
subsystems.role: grounds decisions in the company's own documents and records.

subsystems.name: Action library
subsystems.role: the deterministic skills the agent can invoke instead of guessing.

subsystems.name: Control plane
subsystems.role: keeps the agent inside policy and leaves an audit trail.

buildSteps.title: Map the process
buildSteps.detail: Observe how people actually do the work today — systems touched, decision points, exception rates and volumes — so you know which parts are worth automating.

buildSteps.title: Build the deterministic skeleton
buildSteps.detail: Wire up the ordinary API calls and screen actions first. Automation that can be coded reliably should never be handed to a model.

buildSteps.title: Ground the model
buildSteps.detail: Connect the relevant document stores and systems of record, chunk and embed them, and index them so retrieval respects each user's permissions.

buildSteps.title: Add perception
buildSteps.detail: Plug in document and screen understanding so invoices, emails, PDFs and legacy interfaces become structured fields with confidence scores.

buildSteps.title: Define tools and guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Give the agent a small set of typed actions with strict schemas, spend and access limits, and mandatory validation before anything is written.

buildSteps.title: Orchestrate the agent loop
buildSteps.detail: The agent plans, acts, observes the result, retries or re-plans, and escalates when confidence is low or a rule is hit.

buildSteps.title: Insert human checkpoints
buildSteps.detail: Route high-value or low-confidence steps to a person for approval, and record their decision as training and audit data.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate on a golden set
buildSteps.detail: Replay hundreds of real historical cases and measure task success, wrong actions and cost per case before going live.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Run under orchestration with per-tenant isolation, watch for drift and selector breakage, and keep full traces of every action taken.

prerequisites.tech: Reliable function calling and structured output from LLMs
prerequisites.why: agents can only act safely if the model emits well-formed, validated commands.
retrieval is what stops the agent inventing policy, prices or account details.

pathway.milestone: LLM steps embedded in classical bots — document extraction, email triage, exception summarising
pathway.unlocks: unstructured inputs entering workflows that previously needed a human to read them.

pathway.milestone: agentic orchestration of whole sub-processes with approval queues
pathway.unlocks: automation of judgement-heavy work such as claims or onboarding, under supervision.
less maintenance when interfaces change, and automation aimed at the steps with the best return.

pathway.milestone: verifiable autonomy for regulated back-office work
pathway.unlocks: agents trusted to act without sign-off, provided every decision can be reconstructed and audited.
